name: Flipsky 6374 Battle Hardened KV140
notes: Price $87 without pulley (sale; regular $107), $93 with pulley. Rated 3-12S (stored 3x3.7 to 12x4.2 V). Diameter/length are the nominal 63x74 mm can size from the model name; the page only gives overall lengths incl. shaft (108 mm for 8 mm shaft, 99 mm for 10 mm D-shaft). 14 poles. Flipsky claims 'max torque 8 Nm' but Kt*Imax = 5.8 Nm - the claim is inconsistent with KV and max current. Hall sensors were not explicitly confirmed in the text I retrieved from this page, but the Battle Hardened series is sold as sensored - verify before ordering. Flipsky publishes 'motor resistance 0.05 Ohm' identically for the 140/170/190 KV variants without saying phase or line-to-line, which cannot be true for all windings; stored as published and treated as line-to-line, but treat as +/-50% uncertain (VESC detection reports per-phase R; double it for line-to-line). Listed max current is an e-skate marketing figure with no stated duration and is likely optimistic for sustained use; fine for sub-second reaction-wheel bursts, but magnet/iron saturation may reduce Kt at the top end. Built-in hall sensors give 60-degree-electrical resolution only: OK for VESC hall-start FOC, but low-speed torque is coarser than with an encoder.

name: Xiaomi M365 (Classic) 8.5-inch 36 V 250 W hub motor
notes: Direct-drive (gearless) hub, 30 poles / 15 pole pairs, 27 slots, 100 mm stator. KV 18.55 rpm/V and phase-to-phase resistance are from the ScooterHacking wiki. The wiki writes the resistance as '0.361 mOhm'; that is physically impossible for 0.5 mm wire so it is taken as 0.361 ohm line-to-line (matches the 0.179 ohm per-phase = 0.359 ohm L-L that ODrive measured on a similar-size hoverboard motor). A reseller listing for the 350 W Pro variant gives 600 +/-10 rpm at 36 V (KV 16.7) and '>=14 N.m at 17 A current limit'; 17 A is the stock-controller limit used for max_current_a (no duration published, thermal limit unknown). Kt*17 A = 8.8 Nm, below the listing's 14 Nm claim, so the 17 A is probably battery current, not phase current. Rated 36 V; hobbyists run it on 13S (56 V) with VESC (esk8 thread). mass_kg 3.13 = 6.9 lb assembly with tire (Monster Scooter Parts); bare motor 2.34-2.43 kg without tire (wiki). ESTIMATES: rotor_mass = 60% of total, rotor_radius = tire outer radius (8.5 in), inertia = 0.7*m*r^2, length = 2 in tire width. Price is an old AliExpress listing price seen in search results; used units are far cheaper. Hall sensors are standard on this motor (not stated on the cited pages).

Too slow and heavy for this application (432 rpm at 36 V) unless laced into a rim, which adds a lot of inertia. ESTIMATES: diameter = 214 mm spoke-flange diameter, length = 100 mm O.L.D., rotor_mass = 55% of total, inertia = 0.7*m*r^2 for the bare hub (a 20-inch rim+tire would add roughly 0.05-0.06 kg m^2).
